# [B112] I-116's bimodality diagnostic -- which property does the reseed-twin
# driver fix at process startup: address layout, subject-buffer alignment, or
# scheduling/core state?
#
# Source: docs/dev/measurements/probe_b112_diag.sh + drv_align.c + drv_probe.c
#   + drv_probe2.c + summarize_b112.py + summarize_pipe.py (this commit), run
#   by lane b112bimodal 2026-09-28 09:50-09:56 EDT. Cell: asr-lb-fixed
#   (row11_fixed, pattern `(?<=\xc3\xa9)x`), gcc 15.2.0-16ubuntu1 -O2, orig
#   and reseed-twin, over synth-dense (1 MB) and synth-64k-asc (64 KB, the
#   widest split) -- the SAME binaries [B109]'s multilaunch addendum built
#   (bench d0220be, pcrec pin a32bc86e, workdir /var/tmp/b109twin-htuo1bxs,
#   read-only here; sha256 of bin/row11_fixed_orig_gcc =
#   96076d5ce68c48515948fb3322d3fca8f59f0728c5130baa3636ba30656fdcbe,
#   unchanged from [B109]'s own archive). All new binaries for this probe
#   (the _ctl / _align / _probe / _probe2 / _align64code variants) are built
#   fresh in /var/tmp/b112bimodal-scratch from the SAME row11_fixed*.c
#   sources copied byte-for-byte out of that workdir, with only the DRIVER
#   changed (drv.c -> drv_align.c / drv_probe.c / drv_probe2.c) or the CFLAGS
#   changed (-falign-functions=64 -falign-loops=64); the regex program itself
#   is untouched in every arm. Box: ubuntubudu (AMD Ryzen 5 1600, 12 threads,
#   acpi-cpufreq driver, schedutil governor, ASLR=2/full at the start of this
#   run); load 0.08-0.82 throughout (see per-section `uptime` lines below);
#   NOT gated -- `pgrep -af "pcrecbench (report|run|quick)"` (excluding the
#   grep's own command line, the documented self-match trap) was checked
#   clear immediately before every timed block; no other lane ran a heavy
#   suite concurrently. Command for each experiment is the literal shell
#   loop printed inline in the section header below; NTRIALS=21 throughout
#   (drv.c's own in-process trial count, unchanged from [B109]).
#
# Ask (inbox I-116, pcrecdev1, 2026-09-28 ~10:0x EDT): "if we can do better
# than more launches" for O-68's per-process bimodal timing state --
# (1) ASLR off (setarch -R): do the two modes collapse? (2) subject-buffer
# alignment (top suspect): posix_memalign(4096) + offset sweep, does the
# split follow the offset? (3) counters fast vs slow -- perf is REFUSED on
# this box (perf_event_paranoid=4, no sudo, not attempted); substituted
# with per-launch code/data virtual-address telemetry, per-launch CPU id +
# that CPU's scaling_cur_freq, a taskset single-core pin, and a deliberate
# idle-gap arm. Optional: taskset -c N (done); governor->performance
# (REFUSED: /sys/.../scaling_governor is root:root 0644, `echo performance >`
# and `sudo -n` both refused without a password -- not attempted further,
# per the brief's "governor change needs root, skip it").
#
# ANSWER (read in full below): experiments (1) and the taskset/idle-gap
# additions under (3) together isolate the cause to SCHEDULING / PER-CORE
# DVFS STATE at process start, not address layout and not subject-buffer
# alignment. Sections 3a/3b's telemetry shows fn_mod64 and buf_mod64 are
# CONSTANT (0) on every one of 60+ launches regardless of ASLR mode -- a PIE
# binary's load base is always page-aligned, so a symbol's low-order virtual
# address bits never vary between launches; this rules out intra-page
# code/data placement as a candidate by construction, independent of the
# outcome of experiment (1). Section 3d's per-launch CPU-frequency read
# shows an almost exact match between the observed timing ratio and the
# observed frequency ratio (best_us ~2.5-2.7x slower on "slow" launches;
# freq0_khz ~2.5x lower, ~1.33 MHz vs ~3.30 GHz mean). Section 3e shows
# `taskset -c 3` pinning to a single core removes the slow state entirely
# (0/40 slow launches, both variants) while the SAME command unpinned in the
# same batch still produces it; section 3f shows inserting a 0.3 s idle gap
# between launches (letting the assigned core's frequency decay) raises the
# slow fraction for twin from 0% (back-to-back) to 26.7%. All four lines of
# evidence agree: a process that execs onto a core sitting at a low P-state
# (recently idle, not yet ramped by schedutil) runs its entire ~2-4 ms
# NTRIALS=21 loop before the governor reacts, so the WHOLE launch reads at
# the cold clock; a process landing on an already-warm core reads at the
# boosted clock. This is DRIVER HYGIENE / measurement-protocol territory
# (I-116's own framing), not evidence for pcrec's filed [EMIT-ALIGN] row --
# no code- or data-placement signal we can read correlates with the state,
# and the two placement-invariant channels (fn_mod64, buf_mod64) were
# constant by construction, never varying with the outcome.

############################################################
# VERBATIM: run_diag.sh (sections 0-3c: sanity, ASLR on/off,
# alignment sweep, placement telemetry, code-placement arm)
############################################################
